chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Mansur ibn al-Abbas, from Isma'il ibn Mihran, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:
The woman in ihram should not wear jewelry, and there is no objection to the pattern/design being in the garment itself.

key_terms.الْعَلَمِ: Pattern, design, or motif (often referring to woven designs in fabric)
key_terms.الْمُحْرِمَةُ: The female pilgrim in the state of ihram

ai.seo_question: What jewelry and clothing decorations are permissible for a woman in ihram?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling in *al-Istibsar*, clarifying the distinction between external adornment (*huliy*) and intrinsic fabric decoration (*alam*) for women in ihram. This distinction highlights the Shia juristic focus on whether the item serves as a distinct accessory or is integral to the garment, reflecting broader principles of modesty and ritual purity in Hajj jurisprudence.
